audit.why: Favoured lane (53.11% WR, 789 games): Kassadin is among the weakest pre-6 laners, Vex bullies levels 1-5 freely; the risk is entirely the clock — stacked Riftwalks out-scale her at two-plus items. Difficulty 4/10 fits.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[6].side said 'Skill' while packet levelChart and content win[6] both say Kassadin; the why described a generic anti-dive late game instead of his out-scale.
audit.why: Riftwalk at max rank is a 2s-cooldown blink that stacks bonus damage — late he blinks through the single fear window and bursts her. Rows 0-5 already agree (Vex) across all layers.
audit.corrected: phases[6] flipped to Kassadin 4/10 with a why grounded in stacked Riftwalks; win[6] already 'Kassadin' so side edited alone per chart rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cooldowns field had no numbers; two bleed bullets; missing interactions (Q magic shield absorbs the burst window, W Nether Blade auto-reset as the combo tell) were nowhere on the page.
audit.why: Kit: Riftwalk 5/3.5/2s CD; Q Null Sphere 9-7s with a magic-damage shield; W Nether Blade 7s auto reset; his passive reduces magic damage taken, shaving all of Vex's damage. Note: the kit's 'channel' flag on his Q is a parser misfire — Riot's text says Null Sphere INTERRUPTS channels, it is not itself a channel, so no claim that Vex's fear cancels it was added.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns rewritten with real numbers plus the Q-shield force-out; dos/donts bleed bullets replaced with the auto-reset tell and the stack-chase warning.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving to items — stacked Riftwalks blink past your one fear and the Nether Blade reset deletes you in a pass.

edits.before: Late Vex is anti-engage incarnate: their dive feeds your fears, your R feeds on their deaths.
edits.after: Stacked Riftwalks (2s CD at max) blink through your one fear window — he out-scales you cleanly now.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Personal Space has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s — you never out-wait it; you fight his mana bar and the stack window instead. - Null Sphere (9-7s) shields him against magic: force it out before you commit the burst. - Your W (16s) answers exactly one blink per window.

edits.before: E-mark the contact, Q through the marked line for the fear, auto, walk — every trade he answers with a dash just schedules the next fear.
edits.after: Riftwalk lands him at 500 range for the auto reset — a pulse fired on arrival fears him mid-combo before Nether Blade ever connects.

edits.before: Spending the W pulse on poke spacing and then eating the real engage unfeared — the pulse is the matchup against everything that moves fast.
edits.after: His Riftwalk is 2s at max rank and each cast stacks bonus damage — chase with no fear banked and the third blink turns it around on you.

edits.before: Track Kassadin’s Riftwalk: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: His Q shields him against magic and his passive shaves your damage — force Null Sphere out, then burst the gap.

notes: Rows 0-5 of the chart already agree across packet, full and content (Vex); only row 6 was self-contradictory and is now Kassadin on both layers (win[6] already said Kassadin, side edited alone).
